label: Prairie / wildflower meadow
plain: A mostly native open area with grasses and wildflowers.
source: Texas A&M AgriLife / AECOM 2025 — Grasslands and Prairies
note: Best choice for restored Blackland Prairie, no-mow native meadows, and seeded conservation areas.

label: Wetland / pond edge
plain: A soggy or seasonally wet place that slows water and supports wetland plants.
note: Use only where the site really has wetland or wet-soil function.

label: Woodland / forest
plain: An upland area mostly covered by trees.
source: FEMA 2022 — Forest value reproduced in Texas A&M/AECOM appendix
note: Useful for wooded areas, but this is a national fallback value.

label: Creekside woods
plain: Trees along a creek, drainage, river, or floodplain.
source: FEMA 2022 — Riparian forest value reproduced in Texas A&M/AECOM appendix
note: Use only for wooded creek corridors or floodplain forest.

label: Mostly non-native grass
plain: A grassy area dominated by introduced or exotic grasses.
source: EcoMetrics / Texan by Nature / EOG 2024 — Native vs non-native grass restoration
note: Best available Texas value for non-native grass cover.

label: Mowed turf field
plain: A regularly mowed lawn, field, or turf area.
source: Editable turf-field starting estimate based on Texas non-native grass valuation
note: No clean Central Texas turf ecosystem-service value was found. This starting estimate can be changed if you have better local data.

label: Other open green land
plain: A vegetated open area that is not clearly prairie, wetland, forest, or turf.
source: FEMA 2022 — Rural green open space value reproduced in Texas A&M/AECOM appendix
note: Fallback class only. Pick a more specific category when possible.

label: Urban green open space
source: Texas A&M AgriLife / AECOM 2025 — Urban Green Open Space
note: Broad category with overlap risk. Not recommended as the default for prairie restoration.
